champion: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with associated hematologic malignancy
ordered_diagnoses: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with associated hematologic malignancy

facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes
A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes

concepts.why: The presence of a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells, uniformly positive for CD207/langerin, and negative for myeloperoxidase, is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

The patient's history of chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome, refractory anemia with excess blasts, and prior bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts, supports the diagnosis of myelodysplastic syndrome.
The presence of myeloblasts in the bone marrow biopsy and the identification of pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes, suggests the possibility of acute myeloid leukemia.

concepts.preferred_label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with associated hematologic malignancy
concepts.why: The coexistence of Langerhans cell histiocytosis and myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukemia, suggests a possible association between the two conditions.
The presence of BRAF-V600E variant status identified through immunohistochemical studies explains the uncovered fact.

rationales.F05: The presence of a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells is highly suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F06: Uniform positivity for CD207/langerin is a characteristic feature of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F08: The presence of the BRAF-V600E variant is often associated with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F10: The identification of identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes in both bone marrow and skin biopsy specimens suggests a clonal relationship between the hematologic malignancy and the Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
